name: Mycelium
description: Miles Stevenson's game of dueling fungi on a hexagonal board: place nodes, trigger a confluence from the centre, and spread clusters to convert your rival.
rules: Mycelium is played on a size-5 hex-hex board (61 cells). Player 1 plays black nodes and player 2 plays green nodes; black moves first.
On a normal turn a player places one node on any empty cell. Placing a node in the centre cell (e5) triggers a confluence turn.

A cluster is a connected group of like-colour nodes. A spore cluster has no enemy neighbours; a hyphae cluster touches at least one enemy node. A strand is a straight line of nodes inside a hyphae cluster.

A confluence turn has two phases: first every spore cluster spreads in initiative order, then every hyphae cluster spreads. Initiative starts at 1 and counts up; clusters whose size matches the current initiative may spread.
During each initiative order, if both players have eligible clusters the player who did not start the confluence chooses first and the players alternate until all clusters of that size have spread.

A spore cluster spreads by selecting one of its nodes and tracing a straight line through empty cells to the first enemy node; that source node moves to the enemy node's cell and the enemy node is removed.

A hyphae cluster spreads by selecting one strand and converting up to that many adjacent enemy nodes in a straight line touching the strand. One strand per hyphae cluster may spread in a confluence turn.
Clusters created by conversion may also spread during the same confluence phase, provided their size's initiative order has not yet finished.
After all spreads finish, any node remaining in the centre is removed. A player with no nodes left loses; if both players have no nodes left, the player who initiated the confluence loses.

If neither player has lost, normal play resumes with the player who did not initiate the confluence placing the next node. The game is drawn if 500 plies are played without a confluence ending the game.
